scope.description: One-row deepening tranche for the Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 3 glossy Bilingual Exeggutor insert, emphasizing the October 1 1999 magazine/book route, Dr. Ooyama's bilingual joke-card design, the glossy reprint relationship to the rarer non-glossy 1999 Tropical Mega Battle participation version, and image-level identification traps including the Dr. Ooyama tie/crop difference.

chase_cards.name: Exeggutor [Bilingual] [Glossy]
chase_cards.why: The Trainer Magazine copy is the accessible shadow of one of the great early international prize cards: same bilingual concept, magazine route, glossy finish, and enough image-level differences to make careless matching dangerous.

key_artists.name: Dr. Ooyama / Kouichi Ooyama
key_artists.why: Bulbapedia and PokeBoon credit the print to Dr. Ooyama. That matters twice: as the card's playful bilingual authorship, and as a visible identification feature because the Dr. Ooyama figure/crop differs between Trainer Magazine and Tropical Mega Battle versions.

claims.text: The local catalog models Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 3 insert as a one-row unnumbered promotional source group containing Exeggutor at source index 132.
Bulbapedia's unnumbered promotional list identifies source row 132 as Exeggutor [Bilingual] [Glossy], Grass, distributed through Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 3 insert on October 1, 1999.
PokeBoon identifies the same print as Exeggutor [Bilingual] [Glossy], Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 3, distribution date October 1, 1999, and marks it as a book/unpeeled object.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon credit the Exeggutor promotional print to Dr. Ooyama.
Bulbapedia notes that this Exeggutor is one of only two cards with Japanese text and English translations below it, giving rise to the Bilingual Exeggutor collector name.

Elite Fourum documents that the Trainer Magazine glossy print can be separated from the Tropical Mega Battle non-glossy print by image details around Dr. Ooyama, especially the tie/crop, not only by gloss and color.
The release matters because it made a scarce international-event idea available through a magazine route, while leaving enough variant detail that agents must respect both access and provenance.

Agents should preserve Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 3 route, source index 132, Bilingual / Glossy signal, Dr. Ooyama credit, magazine/book insert identity, and non-equivalence with the non-glossy Tropical Mega Battle participation print before accepting a match.

Preserve row identity as source index 132 and card name Exeggutor [Bilingual] [Glossy].
Confirm glossy / magazine insert / book-unpeeled context where seller evidence allows.
Check Dr. Ooyama credit and compare the Dr. Ooyama figure/crop/tie area when distinguishing from the Tropical Mega Battle print.
Separate the non-glossy Tropical Mega Battle participation version unless provenance and image details support that route.
Separate Evolutions / CP6, standard Exeggutor, Wind from the Sea Exeggutor, and other Exeggutor rows by number, set, stock, and route.
Request front/back photos, stock/gloss evidence, and if sealed/unpeeled, magazine/book context separately from catalog identity.

narrative.human_title: Trainer Magazine Vol. 3 Exeggutor: the bilingual trophy idea comes home in gloss
narrative.why_it_matters: This card is a beautiful little fork in the archive. The non-glossy Tropical Mega Battle version belongs to the Hawaii table, where Japanese and American children met across language. The glossy Trainer Magazine version carries that same bilingual joke-card idea into a reader object. It is more available, but not less meaningful: it shows Media Factory re-circulating tournament magic through the magazine apparatus, and it teaches agents that access route, finish, and even the tiny Dr. Ooyama tie/crop detail can matter as much as the name Exeggutor.

narrative.human_title: Bilingual Exeggutor 132: the glossy copy with a route of its own
narrative.why_it_matters: Collectors chase the Hawaii story, but this magazine print has its own kind of magic. It is a reader-accessible echo of the international table: Japanese and English stacked together, Dr. Ooyama grinning from the art, and a glossy finish that says this object came through Pokemon Card Trainers rather than straight from the Tropical Mega Battle floor. The agent has to care about that distinction because the romance is close enough to mislead you.
